reviews.title: Optimize this for teens please!
reviews.contents:
I got this app and so far I love it. I realized that my teenage daughter needs this more than I do. Unfortunately the school system has zero compassion for the science that says that pre-teens and teens experience a biology shift that causes them to experience later sleep onset and wake times, plus the need for more hours compared to adults (9-11 hours!). All of this, plus a new and thriving social life outside of family wreaks havoc on their sleep schedule. She missed a class from oversleeping and was so stressed and frustrated over her erratic sleep habits she came to me and asked for help, which in all honesty really surprised me! I had literally just started on this app when she did this and couldn’t believe I didn’t think of it for her first. She’s using it now (still on her trial) and we’re willing to see how it does, if it helps, even though it’s for adult sleep needs. She likes the interface and the gamification of reducing her sleep debt. 

She also suggested the ability to edit her “wind down” activity such as “Pack backpack” and “Set next the next day’s school outfit”. She also suggested “spending time with pets” which I thought was actually brilliant given the calming benefits of petting our critters. 

If this app helps my teenager feel rested and more motivated to get to bed at a decent hour than shut up and take my money!

reviews.title: It's Nice, But...
reviews.contents: I really do like how the makers of this app approaches the dynamic of sleep. However, I was finding that AutoSleep possesses the Sleep Debt characteristic, and it also shows the countdown of how much time I have left before I have to wake up (the latter of which is a pretty big deal to me). As for the Watch waking function, at first, I was testing out the difference between using the iPhone to wake me up, but I wasn't a fan of being restricted by only the sounds that the makers of Rise presents. I'd prefer to wake up with my own music that is present on my iPhone (not from Apple Music). The Watch "haptic feedback" tap worked well for me, but then, in the app interface, when you see the wake time initiated on the Watch, that particular time doesn't show up in the timeline on the iPhone or iPad. Instead, you have to initiate the phone's wake time function in order to see it. Lastly, as was said above, it would be very helpful to show a countdown of how much time is left before waking up. That way, when the timer is set, a countdown can be seen on the Watch. Secondly, it appears that the phone wake function and the Watch wake function don't synchronize with each other, which can make it confusing for a first time user to decide which one to use. All in all, this app is quite nice, but frankly, cheaper options are available to help with both Sleep Debt, and with waking. Aside from that, if you desire to see a timeline that shows the effects that workouts and naps have on your overall well being, this might be for you.

reviews.title: Actually accurate, productivity is thriving
reviews.contents: I don’t normally leave written reviews, just the stars. However, I have a major problem with sleeping when most people do. It seems like my body has always done its best when I sleep most of the day and stay up most of the night. I met a night nurse once who helped me realize that some people just function better this way and there’s nothing wrong with this, and it’s silly to expect each and every person to only sleep from 9pm-6am and be busy from 9am-5pm while winding down from 5pm-9pm every evening. So I download rise hoping to stop feeling guilty for staying up most of the evening having productive windows when I wake up around 1pm-3pm and then again from 6pm-9pm. Since I seem to only sleep my best during 5/6am-12pm window, I’m always missing out on “the day” as my parents would say. Now rise is so accurate, they used motion from my phone for 200 nights to find my rhythm and now it tells me when melatonin is highest and to close my eyes to fall asleep, when to schedule my heaviest projects so that I have peak energy during that time also. This is the first time in my life I understand my energy levels and can use it to maximize my productivity and feel less guilty about when I sleep and when I feel tired. Thanks Rise!

reviews.title: I like this app, but for the price, it could be better.
reviews.contents:
I really enjoy this app, but I’m not convinced it’s worth the price. I cancelled before the automatic $60 one and signed up for the $36  one, which is sketchy to not have that as the default to be honest, because I don’t know if there is any difference. 
I use my Fitbit to track my sleep and just import the data, which works really well and eliminates some of the problems I saw other people were having. 
It really is quite a simple app though. My Fitbit is doing most of the heavy lifting and it just does the calculations. I wish it had more features like telling me my ideal wake up time (which it only does on the widget which is annoying) instead of an obscure “wake zone” that gives me no time reference. I’m finding myself using other apps to fill in the gaps that this one is missing like ideal wake up time, sleep quality, habit tracker, etc. If this app had all those things I could see it being worth $60 a year, but I feel even $36 is pushing it for what you get. My Fitbit subscription was $70 a year and does everything else except measure sleep debt. So it doesn’t really add up in my mind. That being said, I am happy I bought a subscription, I really like knowing my sleep debt, I just wish the app developers were more transparent with the pricing and that it had a couple more features.

reviews.title: A tool for conscious time management and sleep health awareness
reviews.contents: This app/service is seriously amazing. It has helped me to understand my behavioral patterns around sleep, energy, and how I manage my time in a way that allows me to take control and use what I have to my advantage. I’ve been able to understand why I feel the way I do, both at different exhaustion levels (through tracking sleep debt) and at different points throughout the day. When I can see it predicted so accurately, I can plan high-impact activities when I’ll be most able to accomplish them, and plan rest at times that will allow me a more comfortable, productive day. I hav noticed a strong correlation between days when my sleep debt is high and when I feel unable to concentrate and stay motivated. Being a human with a cognitive disability (tbi) I already start off behind. It’s been life changing to gain these insights that Rise makes so readily available through tracking sleep and health patterns via phone and my watch. For anyone it’s interesting to learn about. For those with disabilities or challenges around healthy sleep, time management, daytime energy/focus, and staying on a consistent rhythm, this is the only sleep oriented app you need.

reviews.title: No option except to pay (honest review)
reviews.contents:
I saw this app and decided that as a teen who has to wake up at 6am for school every morning, that this could help me out to you know, wake up on time. I did the beginning part and all that and then it asked me to do a free 2 week trial and of course I knew that it would do that, like most apps do. The payment after the trial is what I had a problem with. The yearly payment is so expensive like $70 a year and as someone who can’t pay without getting my parents permission, I can’t use the app at all. On top of that, as I was writing this review after submitting another one before deleting, it told me that they believe money should not be the primary reason not to use rise. There’s no cancel button on the free trial screen so if you don’t pay you can’t even USE the app like at all. So how is that supporting the fact that money shouldn’t be the primary reason hm? I suggest maybe instead of pushing for people to pay/do a free trial, just a few things could be unlocked but a majority of the options you’d have to pay for. That would make this app a total game changer for the people who can’t afford this or are not allowed to waste money something so expensive each year when the money could go towards other things that are necessities. Thank you for taking the time to read this and have a great day/night! 
-❤️Munya❤️

reviews.title: Chronic Fatigue Syndrome/ADHD/AUTISM
reviews.contents: This is great for the community of people with disabilities. For me personally, this has been so helpful to reduce the amount of information I have to think of constantly, struggle with planning around my energy levels and the constant forgetfulness. ADHD and autism pose a significant issue for planning, recall, data processing and attention to time and tasks. Add to this a new diagnosis of chronic fatigue syndrome and it’s a whole overwhelming mess that just left me feeling hopeless and helpless. I used it for the very first night and the day after and I had such a profound experience in knowing what times were suitable for which tasks. I don’t have to keep in mind the time and what I need to focus on next and finding/updating my planner when things don’t align with my energy, etc. I had more satisfaction with my day and my confidence level to take care of my own needs and the visual queues actually capture my brain’s attention + give a small dopamine hit each notification. Feels great feeling in control of my life again. This is the first step towards a personal assistant and one I’ll keep when I require an assistant in the future. Thanks so much, Rise!

reviews.title: False metrics
reviews.contents: I wear an Oura ring and an Apple Watch at night and also track with the Rise app … for 6 months now. This app is bogus IF you compare it with other tracking devices. It works if you have nothing else TO FOCUS YOUR ATTENTION on your sleep/rest hygiene. I suffered from severe insomnia for 2 years after a number of surgeries. I started to actively deal with this problem and have finally gone from almost 20 hours of sleep debt to 0! But Rise still tells me I have multiple hours of debt when I’ve been sleeping 7-8 hours every night with several up to 9 hours for the past 2 months. Utterly bogus. If you are really serious about your health and sleep, and can afford it of course, fork out the money for an OURA ring.  My Apple Watch (not a necessary device for this) and my Oura ring track nearly simultaneously. Rise metrics are never in line with these other 2 devices. What’s wrong with this picture??? The layout of the Rise App is pretty and flashy … but IMO useless. And the other metrics that I get from my ring have really helped me dial in better health. When my Oura ring suddenly alerted me that my body was under severe strain … I listened and went to bed for 2 days straight. In another period I would have ignored it and powered on. I keep a close eye on my HRV and am learning what raises it and what lowers it. So I am NOT a fan of Rise AFTER 6 MONTHS of continuous use.

reviews.title: Unable to edit today’s naps. Finicky smart alarm. Roundabout connection to Garmin.
reviews.contents:
TLDR: Clunky “add nap” function. Confusing labels when editing info for previous days. Smart alarms only function when the app is open or open in the background. Roundabout way to connect with Garmin sleep data; you can’t connect directly with Garmin Connect, you have to connect Garmin Connect with Apple Health, and RISE Sleep pulls data from Apple Health.

Nap function details for devs:
Sometimes I crash in the evening and take a long nap late at night, then get up and do some things before actually getting a full nights sleep. I tried to log this nap before actually going to sleep for the night. I had to use the “today’s add sleep or nap time” function to do this. After entering the nap, the app treated it like a sleep, did its energy levels calculation for the day (which was super squished because it was just a short nap). I was tired and didn’t know how to fix it, so just deleted the log and went to sleep. This morning I tried to use the progress screen to add the nap. I added it to the most recent entry (today’s) because it had the name of the day of the week I was going for. I then realized the way the app works, I needed to add it to the day prior (Thursday night = the DAY of Friday). So I was able to do that. But now, I’m unable to remove the nap I added to today, because the app apparently only lets you add nap times for today, and not remove them? I am able to reduce total nap hours of previous days, so I guess I will have to wait until tomorrow to fix it. Because of this, my energy prediction for the day is inaccurate, and the app thinks I have 0 sleep debt.

reviews.title: Not very useful or accurate
reviews.contents: I feel like this app is only useful for people who don't really need it - people who don't have serious sleep issues and don't have physical or mental health issues that could impact sleep. My main issue is that this app: 1. Applies the same model of an energy cycle to everyone, 2. Takes the input of your sleep times at face value. Both of these are the same reasons why the information that it provides isn't especially useful for anyone with sleep or health problems. In my experience, the estimates of peaks and dips haven't been very accurate, and these peaks and dips could be influenced by some many factors that the app isn't / can't account for. The app also seems to accept average sleep and wake times are the "natural" or "ideal" for that person when in reality things like sleeping and waking very early or very late are likely to be influenced or caused by other circumstances such as a job or a health problem. People who are drawn to an app like rise are probably more likely to suffer from issues that impact their sleep and its quality, and the app doesn't really do anything to pinpoint those issues or how to resolve them, basically just tells you what hours you're "supposed to" have more energy or what hours are estimated to be ideal for sleep based on the limited information its working with.
